observation_summary: Cloning an empty TimeSeries object resulted in an IllegalArgumentException because the clone() method called createCopy(0, -1), which triggered a validation check requiring start <= end.
reasoning_summary: The original implementation of clone() relied on calling createCopy(0, getItemCount() - 1). When the series was empty, getItemCount() returned 0, resulting in a call to createCopy(0, -1). This triggered an IllegalArgumentException in createCopy due to the 'start <= end' check. The fix replaces this logic with a direct clone of the object and a deep clone of the data list, effectively reimplementing the cloning procedure to avoid the invalid range check entirely. This is a correction of the procedure used to perform the clone operation.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows the exception originates from createCopy(0, -1) called by clone().
The fix_diff_oracle shows the removal of the call to createCopy(0, getItemCount() - 1) and its replacement with a direct super.clone() and deepClone of the data list.
The bug report states that cloning an empty TimeSeries causes an IllegalArgumentException.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix avoids the check that was failing, the root cause is the incorrect implementation of the cloning procedure (calling a method with an invalid range) rather than a missing or incorrect validation check itself.
